channel.title: Counter Space
channel.description: Kitchen gear, judged by what it does on a Tuesday night.

item.title: Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?
item.description: They share a name and almost nothing else. The decision is not about which fries better — it is about how you cook on a normal weeknight.

item.title: A no-hype checklist for comparing air fryer capacity
item.description: Quarts are the least honest number on the box. Here is what to check instead, and why the biggest number is often the wrong buy.

item.title: How to assess cleanup and counter-space trade-offs
item.description: The appliance you stop using is the one that is annoying to wash. This is the least glamorous part of the decision and the most predictive.

item.title: Questions to ask before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance
item.description: Every appliance claims ten jobs. The useful question is which two it does well, and whether those two are the jobs you have.

item.title: Instant-read or wireless: which meat thermometer fits your grill?
item.description: One answers "is this done right now?". The other answers "tell me when it is done" while the lid stays shut. The right one depends on how you cook.

item.title: Air fryer vs. toaster oven: which one should you actually buy?
item.description: Same heat, different shape. The choice comes down to whether you cook piles you can shake or trays you leave flat.

item.title: Air fryer for a family of four: how much capacity do you actually need?
item.description: Quarts are the least useful number on the box. Servings are the most misleading one. Here is the question that settles it instead.

item.title: Can you air fry a whole chicken? What to check before you buy
item.description: The answer is decided by one dimension nobody publishes. Here is how to find it, and what to do when the manufacturer has not.

item.title: How hot should chicken be? A temperature guide that does not depend on a timer
item.description: The safe numbers, straight from the USDA chart, plus why colour is the worst thing you can judge chicken by.

item.title: Dishwasher-safe baskets: what the label means before you buy
item.description: The label is about the basket. It says nothing about the coating, the electronics, or the second basket.

item.title: A wireless thermometer for a long cook: what changes, and what it costs you
item.description: Leave-in monitoring is a different product category, not a better version of the same one. Here is the trade in full.

item.title: Where to probe a chicken — and why the wrong spot gives you a wrong answer
item.description: A reading is only as good as the place it came from. Six placement rules, and the one that catches everybody.
